propositions: The s3 doctor's _fold_heads function currently merges bundle heads into the worktree HEAD using git merge, making the heal result dependent on the checked-out branch, which causes _require_tracker_on_ref to refuse all off-branch heals for safety.
The heal should instead fold bundle heads into the published ref's tip (refs/heads/<ref>) using git merge-tree --write-tree and git commit-tree, independent of the worktree's checked-out branch.
The narrower refusal guard should only refuse when the ref IS checked out and the worktree is dirty with tracked changes, allowing off-branch and detached-HEAD trackers to heal successfully.
The tracker's configured merge=ours driver for .bridge_state files must be preserved through the merge-tree mechanism, resolving policy-driven collisions rather than conflicting.
After an on-branch heal, the worktree must be consistent with the moved ref; after an off-branch heal, the checked-out branch and worktree must remain unchanged.

Tests must verify that side-branch and detached-HEAD trackers heal losslessly, the merge policy is honored under merge-tree, and no commit reachable only from a side branch becomes reachable from the published ref.
